20	CASE OD2-DEV-MISLEAD: Checkout payment failures after the v4.12 release
21	
22	Setting: Fernhollow Outfitters is a fictional online outdoor-gear retailer. Its checkout service, checkout-api (16 pods), sends card payments to an external gateway, Quillmark Payments, using API credentials. Since 3 March, roughly one payment attempt in 27 has failed, and the failures come and go. A new checkout release (v4.12) went out that morning, and a spring promotion started the same day. Engineering wants to roll the release back, and Finance wants a revenue-impact figure for the board.
23	
24	Presenting request: The Head of Engineering asks: what is causing the intermittent payment failures since 3 March, should we approve the full rollback of checkout-api v4.12, and what should we do now?
25	
26	INITIAL EVIDENCE
27	E1 [stage S1] Incident ticket INC-4471, checkout on-call (system-record): INC-4471 opened 3 March 11:20 by paging alert checkout_payment_failure_rate (rule: 30-minute failure rate at least 2% AND at least 40 failed attempts). Daily payment-attempt failure rate, checkout-api: 28 Feb 0.4%, 1 Mar 0.4%, 2 Mar 0.5%, 3 Mar 3.4%, 4 Mar 3.9%, 5 Mar 3.6%, 6 Mar 3.8%. All new failures carry error code PAYMENT_UPSTREAM_REJECTED. On-call summary: 'Intermittent. A customer fails, retries a few minutes later, often succeeds.' No pod restarts and no gateway timeouts recorded.
28	E2 [stage S1] Email from Dara Okonjo, Engineering Manager, Checkout, 6 March (manager-account): Subject: INC-4471, we know what this is. v4.12 shipped 3 March at 10:40 and the alert fired forty minutes later. The failure rate went from half a percent to nearly four overnight and has stayed there. v4.12 replaced our gateway HTTP client and connection-pool settings, which is exactly the code path that's failing. Quillmark's status page is green, so it isn't them. I want approval to roll the whole fleet back to v4.11 tonight and freeze checkout releases until we've rewritten the client. Dara
29	E3 [stage S1] Release notes, checkout-api v4.12 (CHG-2214) (change-record): checkout-api v4.12, deployed 3 March 10:40, CHG-2214, approved by Engineering CAB. Changes: (1) Gateway client moved to a new HTTP library; connection pool size raised from 50 to 64. (2) Error handling: every non-2xx response from the payment gateway now maps to one code, PAYMENT_UPSTREAM_REJECTED. The raw upstream status is no longer logged at INFO level. The customer message is unchanged: 'Your card was declined. Please try another card or try again.' (3) Security: partial card numbers previously written to debug logs are now masked, closing audit finding SEC-2291 (remediation deadline 13 March). A rollback to v4.11 reverts all three changes.
30	E4 [stage S1] Quillmark Payments status page capture and support ticket TS-90412 (vendor-account): Quillmark status page, captured 6 March 08:00: 'All systems operational' for Authorisation API, Search API and Merchant Dashboard on every day from 1 to 6 March; no incidents posted. Support ticket TS-90412, Quillmark reply of 5 March: 'We see no platform-wide incidents during the period. Our records show your requests are reaching us. Please review your integration and confirm you are handling all documented response codes.'
31	E5 [stage S1] Email from Priya Halvorsen, CFO, 6 March (leadership-account): Gross online revenue for the week to 6 March is down 9% on the prior week. The prior week did include the final days of Winter Clearance, which ended 1 March, and Spring Trail Sale launched on 3 March, but I'm clear in my mind that the checkout failures are what cost us. I need a figure for the board pack on Monday, and I expect us to restate the Q1 forecast on the back of it.
32	E6 [stage S1] Customer Care lead Tomasz Reyes, notes for INC-4471 bridge call, 5 March (staff-account): 238 customer contacts since 3 March about declined cards. Most say the decline came 'out of nowhere' and that a retry a few minutes later worked. Eleven customers phoned their bank. In nine of those cases the bank said it had no record of any authorisation attempt at the time of the failure. Agents have been advising customers to try a different card.

2	Title: Quillmark API usage report for credential fernhollow-prod-01, 1–6 March
3	Source: Quillmark account team (vendor-account)
4	
5	Prepared 6 March. Credential fernhollow-prod-01. Rate limit: 300 requests/minute per credential, all endpoints combined. 1–2 March: /v2/payments peaked at 52/min; /v2/transactions/search near zero in the daytime, with one nightly run at 02:00 (about 1,900 calls over 9 minutes). From 3 March 09:00: /v2/transactions/search bursts of 360–430/min in the first 3–4 minutes of each quarter hour, 09:00–21:00, user-agent 'settle-recon/2.3'. /v2/payments steady at 30–58/min. HTTP 429 responses: 0 on 1–2 March; 4,980–6,310 per day on 3–6 March, all within burst minutes, header X-RateLimit-Scope: credential. Issuer declines steady at 0.3–0.4% of payments. Temporary limit increases take 3–5 business days and are chargeable.

input.brief:
The failures are not caused by release v4.12. They come from Finance's settle-recon job, which has run every 15 minutes from 09:00 to 21:00 since 3 March (FIN-CHG-0187). It shares a gateway credential with checkout. Each run sends 360–430 search calls a minute, and the credential's limit is 300 a minute across all calls. Quillmark then returns 429 errors to checkout payments in those minutes. The v4.12 error handling shows all of these as "card declined".

The evidence for this is strong:
- 93% of failures fall in the first minutes of each quarter hour.
- Failures began at 09:00, before the 10:40 deploy.
- Failures stopped during the finance maintenance window on 6 March.
- Half the pods were rolled back to v4.11 in a test, and they failed at the same rate. 341 of their 351 failures were 429s.

Next steps:
1. Revert settle-recon to nightly, or pause its daytime runs. Then confirm the 429 rate and payment failures fall.
2. Don't roll back v4.12. A rollback wouldn't fix the failures and would reintroduce the SEC-2291 card-number logging problem.
3. Give settle-recon its own credential before any daytime schedule returns.
4. Fix the error mapping so 429s aren't shown as declines.
5. Don't attribute the 9% revenue drop to the failures yet. Conversion and order value also fell, the promotion changed traffic mix, and a roughly 3% failure rate can't explain 9% on its own. Measure the real lost revenue from failed attempts that were never retried successfully.
